author: PavelMakarchuk
body:
**The TY2021 mirror confirms the convention difference end-to-end.** PE books each rebate to the year whose liability determines it; TAXSIM subtracts it in the payout year. The same rebates therefore appear as **PE-lower** flat clusters in TY2021 and **PE-higher** in TY2022:

| State | TY2021 (assessment yr, PE applies) | TY2022 (payout yr, TAXSIM applies) | Rebate |
|---|---|---|---|
| VA | −$486 med, 98% PE-lower (n=80) | +$250/$500 | capped at 2021 liability |
| MA | −$718, 97% (n=116) | +$1,890 | 62F = 14.0312% of 2021 liability |
| ME | **−$850 exactly**, 100% (n=51) | +$850 | $850 relief |
| GA | −$375, 99% (n=102) | +$375 | surplus refund |
| NM | −$1,293, 100% (n=122) | +~$500/$1,000 | 2021-liability rebates |
| HI | −$410, 100% (n=126) | +$300 | Act 115 |
| CO | −$758, 82% (n=94) | Cash Back | 2021 TABOR |
| IL | −$100, 99% (n=117) | — | 2021-liability rebate |

TY2021 flat clusters: −$500×106, −$250×81, −$800×54, −$1,300×37, −$850×24, −$750×24.

Because the difference is a *timing* one, it **hits the match rate twice** — once in each year, opposite signs — so settling the convention (#716) recovers alignment in both 2021 and 2022 at once. Exception: **ID** has no 2021 mirror (its 2022 rebates keyed to 2020/2019 liability, so PE books them before our window). Alongside the VA-2025↔2024 mirror already documented, every payout-year cluster now has its assessment-year counterpart located.
